Let \( ABC \) be an isosceles triangle with \( AB = AC \). Points \( P \) and \( Q \) are located inside triangle \( ABC \) such that \( BP = PQ = QC \). Suppose that \( \angle BAP = 20^\circ \), \( \angle PAQ = 46^\circ \), and \( \angle QAC = 26^\circ \). Compute the measure of \( \angle APC \) in degrees.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let all angles be measured in degrees.

Set

\[
AB=AC=1,\qquad AP=p,\qquad AQ=q,\qquad BP=PQ=QC=x.
\]

Since

\[
\angle BAP=20^\circ,\quad \angle PAQ=46^\circ,\quad \angle QAC=26^\circ,
\]

we have

\[
\angle PAC=46^\circ+26^\circ=72^\circ.
\]

By the Law of Cosines in \(\triangle ABP,\triangle APQ,\triangle AQC\),

\[
x^2=1+p^2-2p\cos20^\circ,
\]

\[
x^2=p^2+q^2-2pq\cos46^\circ,
\]

\[
x^2=1+q^2-2q\cos26^\circ.
\]

Equating the last two expressions and simplifying gives

\[
q=\frac{1-p^2}{2(\cos26^\circ-p\cos46^\circ)}. \tag{1}
\]

Equating the first and second expressions gives

\[
q^2-2pq\cos46^\circ+2p\cos20^\circ-1=0. \tag{2}
\]

One checks that the system is solved by

\[
p=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ},\qquad q=\frac{\sin40^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

Indeed, using product-to-sum identities,

\[
2(\cos26^\circ-p\cos46^\circ)
=\frac{\cos18^\circ}{\sin74^\circ},
\]

and

\[
1-p^2=\frac{\sin72^\circ\sin40^\circ}{\sin^2 74^\circ},
\]

so (1) gives \(q=\frac{\sin40^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}\).

Also,

\[
\sin^2 74^\circ-\sin^2 40^\circ
=\sin66^\circ\sin34^\circ,
\]

and

\[
\cos20^\circ\sin74^\circ-\cos46^\circ\sin40^\circ
=\frac12\sin66^\circ,
\]

which verifies (2). Hence in the required configuration,

\[
AP=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

Now consider \(\triangle APC\). We know

\[
AC=1,\qquad \angle PAC=72^\circ,\qquad AP=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

A triangle with angles \(72^\circ,74^\circ,34^\circ\) and side \(AC=1\) has

\[
AP=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}
\]

by the Law of Sines. Therefore \(\triangle APC\) is congruent to that triangle, so

\[
\angle APC=74^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{74}
\]
